name: squish-switch
title: Squish Switch
description: A row of preference switches in a dark card. Each pill flips on click or drag, and its round thumb stretches along the track as it moves, then squashes back when it lands.
use: A settings or preferences list wants a switch that feels tactile and can also be dragged, not just clicked.
avoid: The squish needs motion to read; reduced-motion users get a plain instant swap and lose the character.
a11y: A native switch role with aria-checked and a label prop. The outline is removed with no replacement, so keyboard focus is invisible. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A rounded dark card holds three stacked rows, each with a title, a smaller grey hint and a wide pill switch on the right. Off switches are dark grey with a pale round thumb at the left; on switches turn near-white with a dark thumb at the right.
behaves: Clicking or dragging the switch flips it and the thumb springs to the other end. Faster flicks stretch the thumb along the direction of travel, it squashes on landing, and hovering swells it slightly while dragging lets it follow the finger.
customise: Track, on-track, thumb and on-thumb colours, plus width, height, radius, spring speed, stretch amount and hover scale are props. The label is a prop; the card around it belongs to the demo.
weight: light: Two springs and a motion value per switch; nothing runs once it settles.
demo: Three preference rows: Push notifications, Weekly digest and Focus mode, each with a one-line hint.
issues: No visible focus ring: outline-none is set with no replacement.
polishWhy: Springy motion sells the squish and the card is tidy; the missing focus ring is the one real flaw.
